Until the customer relationship ends
Until the FIU closes its investigation
At least five years
quiz.explanation: Module FC requires banks to retain all relevant details of STRs submitted to the authorities for at least five years. The FIU's case status does not set the period.

sessions.title: The Bank's Programme: MLRO, Governance, Records and CBB Enforcement
sessions.summary: Get Pearlgate ready for the CBB's examination: board-approved systems and controls, the MLRO and deputy MLRO, AML KPIs, the annual review of effectiveness, record keeping, staff awareness, the CBB's enforcement powers and what its annual reports say about enforcement.
objectives: Describe the board's and senior management's responsibilities for the AML/CFT programme under Module FC
State the main requirements for appointing the MLRO and deputy MLRO and the MLRO's responsibilities
Apply Module FC's record-keeping periods and access requirements
Explain the CBB's enforcement powers for breaches of Module FC and how examinations test the programme

cards.title: Ten days to the examination
cards.setting: Executive floor, Pearlgate head office. 8:00 am.

lines.text: I'm Khalid, chief executive. The CBB's Compliance Directorate arrives in ten days. Tell me plainly: what will they test, and where are we weak?
They'll test whether our controls work, not just whether we have documents: CDD files, monitoring, STR decisions, records and governance.
And governance means me and the board?
It does. Module FC asks the board to approve and review our AML systems and controls every year, and to act on the annual review findings.
We also need to show that AML performance counts in staff appraisals and pay. Module FC asks for KPIs.
This is the final stage before the boss fight: the Boardroom. Let's make sure every piece of the programme stands up.

scenes.heading: The board
scenes.narration: The board approves the bank's documented AML and CFT systems and controls and reviews them every year. The CBB can ask to see that approval and review.

scenes.heading: The MLRO
scenes.narration: An approved, senior MLRO, with at least one deputy, runs the policies, handles internal and external reports and reports on effectiveness.

scenes.heading: Accountability
scenes.narration: AML key performance indicators feed into staff appraisals and pay, so compliance breaches have consequences.

scenes.heading: Records
scenes.narration: Identity, transaction, compliance, report and training records are kept for at least five years and can be produced quickly.

scenes.heading: Review and enforcement
scenes.narration: Effectiveness is reviewed every year. If the bank breaches Module FC, the CBB can impose penalties and other enforcement measures.

cards.title: Who owns AML/CFT at Pearlgate
cards.caption: Responsibility for compliance stays with the bank and the designated MLRO even when tasks are delegated.

items.label: Board of directors
items.detail: Approves and reviews the AML/CFT systems and controls every year and commissions remedial action.

items.label: Senior management
items.detail: Receives the MLRO's effectiveness reports and resources the programme.

items.label: MLRO and deputy MLRO
items.detail: Run policies, decide on STRs, monitor high-risk accounts and keep records.

items.label: All staff
items.detail: Apply CDD, monitor, report suspicion and meet their AML KPIs.

cards.back: The MLRO is an approved person and must be approved by the CBB before appointment.
The role must not be combined with conflicting functions such as internal auditor or business line head.
Not allowed: the MLRO must be a director or employee of the bank.
A member of senior management, free from business-line interference, with direct access to the board and full access to transaction and CDD data.
The MLRO must be resident in Bahrain.
At least one deputy MLRO, also CBB-approved, must be appointed to act in the MLRO's absence.
A permanent replacement, approved by the CBB, within 120 calendar days, with CBB-approved interim arrangements.

cards.question: Pearlgate's MLRO resigns unexpectedly. What does Module FC require?
options: Leave the post empty until the next board meeting
Ask the head of internal audit to take over permanently
Make immediate CBB-approved interim arrangements and appoint a CBB-approved permanent replacement within 120 calendar days
Outsource the role to a consultancy until a replacement is found
cards.explanation: Module FC requires immediate interim arrangements, including an acting MLRO, approved by the CBB, and a permanent replacement within 120 calendar days after CBB approval. Internal audit is a conflicting function and outsourcing is not allowed.

cards.title: Records Module FC expects you to keep
cards.body:
Module FC builds on the record-keeping duties in the AML Law. Conventional banks must keep, for at least **five years**:

- **Customer records:** identity evidence and relationship records, such as application forms, account files, correspondence and the results of any analysis of unusual transactions, counted from when the relationship ends.
- **Transaction records:** documents, including customer instructions by letter, fax or email, that allow the transaction to be reconstructed, counted from when it was completed.
- **Compliance records:** reports produced for the annual compliance review, reports made to or by the MLRO, and records of how each was dealt with.
- **Training records:** dates of AML/CFT training, its nature and the names of staff who took it.

All of these must be available for **prompt and swift access** by the relevant authorities.

cards.title: When does the five-year clock start?
cards.prompt: Match each record to the event that starts its minimum five-year retention period.

pairs.right: When the customer relationship ends
When the transaction was completed
When the transaction was completed
Kept for at least five years after they are submitted
Kept for at least five years as compliance records

lines.text: HR's training lead drops by with a spreadsheet of courses.
Module FC has a chapter on staff training and recruitment, and the MLRO is responsible for keeping arrangements for staff awareness and training in place.
Who decides which staff take what, and when?
Our board-approved policy does, based on our risk assessment and roles. The CBB's risk assessment guidance says training should reflect the findings of that assessment.
And the examiners will ask for proof?
They can. We keep records of dates, content and names for at least five years. And Module FC expects our systems to include adequate screening when we hire.

cards.title: The branch with no reports
cards.situation: Noora's annual effectiveness figures show that the Riffa branch, one of Pearlgate's busiest for cash, made no internal suspicious transaction reports all year, while similar branches made several. The branch manager says this proves his customers are low risk and asks that the figure be left out of the board report.

choices.text: Keep the figure in the report, review a sample of Riffa's cash activity and CDD files, give the branch targeted awareness sessions and tell the board what was found and done.
choices.outcome: Best. Breaking figures down by branch exists to show whether a reasonable overall total hides under-reporting in one part of the bank. The board needs the facts so it can commission remedial measures.

choices.text: Leave the figure out, since zero reports is not a breach in itself.
choices.outcome: Poor. Hiding the figure defeats the purpose of the review and denies the board information it needs to act.

choices.text: Set a target of a minimum number of internal reports per branch each quarter.
choices.outcome: Partly right on the concern, but quotas encourage defensive, low-quality reports rather than real suspicion.

choices.text: Report the branch manager to the CBB immediately for failing to report.
choices.outcome: Poor. There is no evidence yet of a failure to report; the first step is to examine the branch's activity and controls.

cards.title: CBB enforcement by its conventional banking supervisors
cards.caption: All taken under Article 38 of the CBB Law. The reports do not name the banks or say how many concerned AML.

items.label: Actions in 2021
items.detail: Enforcement actions, including financial penalties, reported in the CBB's 2021 annual report.

items.label: Actions in 2022
items.detail: Enforcement actions against banks, including financial penalties, in the 2022 report.

items.label: Actions in 2023
items.detail: Enforcement actions against licensees, including penalties, in the 2023 report.

items.label: Actions in 2024
items.detail: Enforcement actions, including penalties, in the draft 2024 annual report.

cards.title: Whose job is it?
cards.prompt: Sort each task to the person or body Module FC gives it to.

items.text: Approving and annually reviewing the AML/CFT systems and controls
Receiving the annual review reports and commissioning remedial measures
Deciding whether an internal report becomes an external STR
Producing annual reports on the effectiveness of AML/CFT controls
Ongoing monitoring of what may be high-risk customer accounts
Reporting suspicion promptly through the internal procedure
Meeting AML key performance indicators that count in appraisals

cards.question: Without a court order, what fine can the CBB levy on a licensee that fails to comply with Module FC, under the copy of Section FC-9.1 that could be opened?
options: Up to BD 20,000, at the CBB's discretion, in addition to other enforcement measures
Up to BD 1,000, and only after a court ruling
A fixed BD 100 a day until the breach ends, with nothing else
No fine: the CBB can only issue warnings
cards.explanation: Section FC-9.1 allows the CBB, without a court order and at its discretion, to levy a fine of up to BD 20,000 for failure to comply with the module, without prejudice to penalties under the CBB Law, Decree-Law No. 4 or the Penal Code. Module EN sets out other measures.

cards.title: From the CBB's own reports: what enforcement looks like
cards.body:
The CBB rarely names banks it penalises in its annual reports, but it describes the scale and basis of its work:

- Its conventional banking supervision directorates reported **10 enforcement actions** in 2021, **5** in 2022 and **15** in 2023, including financial penalties, all under **Article 38 of the CBB Law**. The draft 2024 report records **two**.
- The **Compliance Directorate** runs onsite AML/CFT examinations that test procedures, systems and internal controls against the AML Law, the CBB Law and Module FC.
- Module FC itself allows the CBB to fine a licensee **up to BD 20,000** without a court order for breaching the module, and points to Module EN for other measures.

The lesson for Khalid's board: enforcement is a regular supervisory tool in Bahrain, and examinations look for evidence that controls work.

cards.title: Getting ready for a CBB examination
cards.body:
- Have the **board-approved** AML/CFT documents and the record of the last annual review ready.
- Pull **sample CDD files** across risk levels, including PEPs, non-residents and corporates with beneficial owners.
- Show the **monitoring** set-up, how alerts are cleared and the investigation records.
- Produce the **internal and external report** figures, with reasons for every internal report not filed.
- Show **training and awareness records** and AML KPIs in appraisals.
- Check that every record can be retrieved **quickly**.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: The board approves and reviews the AML/CFT systems and controls every year and acts on review findings; the CBB can ask to see this.
The MLRO is a CBB-approved, Bahrain-resident senior manager with at least one approved deputy; the role cannot be outsourced or combined with conflicting duties.
AML KPIs must count in staff appraisals and pay, and systems and controls should include adequate screening when hiring.
Keep customer, transaction, compliance, report and training records for at least five years, ready for swift access.
The CBB can fine up to BD 20,000 for Module FC breaches without a court order and takes regular enforcement actions under Article 38 of the CBB Law.

cards.prompt: If a CBB examiner asked you tomorrow to show how you apply your bank's AML procedures in your role, what evidence could you produce, and where would it be stored?

quiz.question: What does Module FC require of the board regarding the bank's AML/CFT systems and controls?
options: They are approved by the MLRO alone and only noted by the board
They are approved by the CBB and adopted automatically by the bank
Documented, then approved and reviewed by the board every year
They are approved once at licensing and need no further board involvement
quiz.explanation: Section FC-2.1 requires the systems and controls to be documented and approved and reviewed annually by the board, and the documentation and board review to be available to the CBB on request.

quiz.question: Which combination of roles does Module FC rule out for the MLRO?
options: MLRO who is also a member of senior management
MLRO combined with the internal auditor role
MLRO who delegates some tasks within the bank
MLRO combined with the compliance officer role in a small bank
quiz.explanation: Module FC bars combining the MLRO with functions that create conflicts, such as internal auditor or business line head. It allows combining with the compliance officer role where the business is limited, and delegation within the bank.

quiz.question: Which requirement applies to Pearlgate's MLRO under Module FC?
options: The MLRO must be resident in Bahrain
The MLRO must be a Bahraini national
The MLRO must hold a law degree
The MLRO must report to the head of retail banking
quiz.explanation: Module FC requires the MLRO to be resident in Bahrain, part of senior management and free from business-line interference. Nationality and a law degree are not stated requirements, and reporting to a business head would undermine independence.

quiz.question: How many deputy MLROs must a conventional bank appoint under Module FC?
options: One for every branch the bank operates
At least one, more if scale and complexity require
None, unless the CBB asks for one
Exactly two, one for retail and one for corporate business
quiz.explanation: Module FC requires at least one deputy MLRO, with more where scale and complexity demand. The deputy is a controlled function and also needs CBB approval.

quiz.question: Pearlgate's AML policy includes KPIs for staff. What does Module FC say about them?
options: KPIs must be published in the bank's annual report
AML KPI results must count in appraisals and pay
KPIs apply only to the compliance department
KPIs are optional and should not affect pay
quiz.explanation: Section FC-2.1 requires KPIs to ensure compliance by all staff, with performance adequately reflected in annual evaluations and remuneration, and the guidance suggests adjusting bonuses for AML breaches.

quiz.question: A customer's account was closed four years ago. A transaction investigation from the account's last month is requested by the authorities. Must Pearlgate still have the identity records?
options: No: identity records can be destroyed when the account closes
Only if an STR was filed on the customer
Yes: they must be kept five years after the relationship ends
No: only transaction records survive after closure
quiz.explanation: Module FC and Article 5 of the Decree-Law require identity evidence and relationship records for at least five years after the relationship ends, so four years after closure they must still exist.

quiz.question: Which training-related record does Module FC require banks to keep for at least five years?
options: Only the cost of external training courses
Each employee's personal test scores published to all staff
Copies of every trainer's CV
When training was given, what it covered and who attended
quiz.explanation: Section FC-7.1 requires records showing when AML/CFT training was given, what it covered and who received it, kept for at least five years.

quiz.question: Which of these is the MLRO responsible for under Section FC-4.2 of Module FC?
options: Annual reports on how well the AML/CFT controls work
Approving the bank's credit facilities above a set limit
Signing off the bank's audited financial statements
Setting the bank's interest rates on deposits
quiz.explanation: The MLRO's listed responsibilities include policies and procedures, compliance with the AML Law, handling internal and external reports, staff awareness and training arrangements, annual effectiveness reports, monitoring high-risk accounts and records.

quiz.question: Under the copy of Section FC-9.1 that could be opened, which statement about CBB penalties for breaching Module FC is correct?
options: Fines for Module FC breaches are paid to the FIU
The CBB can fine only after the Public Prosecution obtains a conviction
A breach of Module FC can lead only to a private warning letter
The CBB may fine up to BD 20,000 without a court order
quiz.explanation: Section FC-9.1 lets the CBB levy fines of up to BD 20,000 at its discretion without a court order, alongside penalties under the CBB Law, Decree-Law No. 4 and the Penal Code, and other measures in Module EN.

quiz.question: What do Module FC's systems and controls requirements expect of hiring practices?
options: Adequate screening to ensure high hiring standards
Hiring only staff who already hold AML qualifications
Rotation of all customer-facing staff every year
Approval of every new employee by the CBB
quiz.explanation: Section FC-2.1 says systems and controls should cover staff training and adequate screening procedures to ensure high standards when hiring. CBB approval applies to approved persons such as the MLRO, not every employee.

regulators: Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB), Compliance Directorate
National Centre for Financial Intelligence, Ministry of Interior (Bahrain's FIU; Financial Intelligence Directorate in the Rulebook text)

bank.question: A Pearlgate customer moves funds she believes come from her brother's smuggling business into a property in her own name, but she never asked him directly. Which assessment fits Decree-Law No. 4 of 2001?
options: She is protected, because property purchases are outside the definition of a transaction
She cannot commit the offence, because only her brother committed the underlying crime
She may commit money laundering, as reason to believe is enough
She commits only a related offence, because she did not carry out the smuggling herself
bank.explanation: Article 2 covers acquiring or using proceeds while knowing, believing or having reason to know or believe they are criminal, and a conviction for the underlying crime is not needed. Property purchases are transactions under the law's broad definition.

bank.question: During an investigation, Pearlgate receives an order obtained by the enforcement unit to deliver account records. A branch officer delays because the customer is 'important'. What is the main legal risk for the officer?
options: Only a CBB fine on the bank, since staff cannot commit offences under the AML law
A related offence of obstructing an investigation order
None, because orders are addressed to the bank, not to individual staff
Breach of customer confidentiality if he does produce the records
bank.explanation: Article 2.6(b) makes failing or refusing to follow, or obstructing, such an order a related offence, and Article 7 removes the secrecy plea. Individuals, not only the bank, can be liable.

bank.question: A senior manager says that because the 2017 amendment dealt with terrorist financing, Decree-Law No. 4 of 2001 no longer governs money laundering. What is the correct position?
options: Money laundering is now covered only by the CBB Rulebook, not by any law
The 2017 decree repealed the 2001 law and replaced it with a new combined AML/CFT law
The 2001 law now applies only to non-bank institutions
The 2001 law still governs ML; 2017 only rewrote the TF offence
bank.explanation: Decree-Law No. 36 of 2017 replaced paragraph (1-3) of Article 3 of the 2001 law, covering the terrorist financing offence. The 2001 law, as amended, still sets the money laundering offence and institutions' duties.

bank.question: Which statement best describes the legal status of Module FC for a conventional bank licensee?
options: It is a Ministry of Interior regulation enforced by the FIU
It is voluntary best practice that banks may adopt if they choose
It applies only to banks that are listed on the stock exchange
A binding CBB directive issued under the CBB Law
bank.explanation: Module FC describes itself as the CBB's directive on combating money laundering and terrorist financing, issued under Article 38 of the CBB Law and applicable to all conventional bank licensees.

bank.question: Pearlgate's board asks which authority prosecutes money laundering cases in court under the Decree-Law. Which answer is correct?
options: The CBB's Compliance Directorate
The Public Prosecution
The bank's MLRO, as the main contact point
The Policy Committee
bank.explanation: Article 4.6 gives the Public Prosecution responsibility for proceedings before the courts. The CBB supervises, the Policy Committee sets policy and the MLRO reports suspicion.

bank.question: Which statement about Article 5 of the Decree-Law and internal controls is accurate?
options: Banks must follow the regulator's instructions on controls, compliance officers and audit
Banks may choose whether to appoint compliance officers at all, based on their size and business model
Only the CBB's own staff may audit a bank's AML controls
Internal controls are a matter for each board and are not mentioned in the law
bank.explanation: Article 5(e) and (g) require compliance with the relevant entities' instructions on policies, procedures, controls, management-level compliance officers and audit functions, and a procedure to audit compliance.

bank.question: A Pearlgate trainee reads the 2023 CBB-hosted copy of Module FC and finds paragraphs dated 'XX 2023' next to text marked as deleted. What is the sensible approach?
options: Ignore all paragraphs in that copy, because consultation copies have no value
Assume every paragraph in the copy is in force exactly as printed
Treat it as amendment text and confirm the in-force wording first
Apply whichever version of the paragraph is less strict
bank.explanation: The CBB-hosted 2023 copy was issued with amendments and shows changed text. It is useful evidence of the rules, but the current Rulebook is the authority for in-force wording.

bank.question: Which statement about Bahrain's role in the international AML system is supported by the CBB's compliance pages?
options: Bahrain is a full individual member of FATF and chairs it permanently
Bahrain left MENAFATF when it joined the GCC
Bahrain has never been subject to a mutual evaluation
It founded and hosts MENAFATF; FATF approved its evaluation in 2018
bank.explanation: The CBB states that Bahrain is a founding member of MENAFATF and hosts its secretariat, participates in FATF through the GCC's membership, and that its mutual evaluation was approved by FATF in June 2018.

bank.question: Pearlgate plans to launch an app-only account. Under the CBB's risk-based approach, when should the ML/TF risks of this new delivery channel be assessed?
options: At the next three-yearly review of the bank's risk assessment
Never, because digital channels are covered by cyber security rules instead
Only after the first suspicious transaction report on the new product has been filed
Before launch, and then kept under review
bank.explanation: The CBB's guidance says risks should be assessed before new products, business practices or relationships are introduced and kept up to date. Waiting for an STR or a later review is too late.

bank.question: Two banks rate the same customer type differently: one 'high', one 'medium'. According to the CBB's risk assessment guidance, is this necessarily wrong?
options: No: ratings depend on each bank's context
Yes: all banks must rate every customer type as high risk
Yes: the CBB publishes fixed ratings that every bank must use
No: ratings are irrelevant because CDD is the same for everyone
bank.explanation: The guidance notes that the same risk may be high in one institution and low in another depending on context. Ratings drive proportionate controls, so CDD is not identical for everyone.

bank.question: A retail customer's identity can be confirmed through the national E-KYC application. Under Module FC, what is the role of document copies?
options: They replace E-KYC for Bahraini nationals
They are never allowed for retail banks
A fallback where E-KYC is not practical
They are always required in addition to E-KYC for every customer
bank.explanation: For retail banks, Module FC verifies name, date of birth and address through the national E-KYC application, and uses current official documents or statements where that is not practical.

bank.question: A customer posts copies of his passport after an initial meeting, certified by a notary in a FATF member state. What else must Pearlgate do under Module FC?
options: Verify the certifier, for example via a professional body or direct contact
Nothing more, because a notary's certification is conclusive
Reject the copies, because only bank staff may certify documents
Ask the CBB to confirm the notary's registration
bank.explanation: Module FC allows certification by listed professionals from GCC or FATF states, who must give clear contact details, and requires the bank to verify the certifier's identity through membership checks, databases or direct contact.

bank.question: A private company's structure shows a holding company owned 60% by a trust. What does Module FC expect Pearlgate to establish?
options: The ultimate owner, funder and controller, including the trust's parties
Only the name of the holding company, since it is the direct shareholder on the share register
Only the trustee, because trustees control trusts
Only the directors listed in the commercial registration
bank.explanation: Module FC requires enquiries into the structure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, provider and controller of funds, and for trusts the settlor, trustees and beneficiaries, including any other potential beneficiaries.

bank.question: A company under formation opened an account at stage one and has not completed its KYC after the agreed period, and it is not cooperating. What does Module FC require?
options: Classify it as dormant and notify the commerce ministry
Transfer the balance to the CBB for safekeeping
Close the account immediately and pay the balance to the founders in cash
Make the account fully operational, since six months have passed
bank.explanation: Module FC requires the account of a non-cooperating company under formation that misses the agreed period to be classified as dormant, with notification to the Ministry of Industry and Commerce; closure is then at the bank's discretion.

bank.question: Pearlgate cannot verify a new customer and has strong doubts about the funds he deposited. Which response best matches Module FC's incomplete-CDD rule?
options: Ask the customer to sign an indemnity and proceed
Keep the account open and let the customer transact while documents are chased
Consider freezing the funds and filing an STR
Return the funds in any convenient form and close the file
bank.explanation: Module FC lists freezing funds and filing an STR among the options where CDD cannot be completed. Where suspicion exists, returning funds without reporting could help the customer move criminal money.

bank.question: A Pearlgate retail customer is non-resident. Which statement about the services offered is consistent with Module FC?
options: Tell the customer which services may be limited
Non-resident customers need no enhanced due diligence if they are salaried
Non-resident customers may only hold accounts in Bahraini dinars
Non-resident customers must be offered every product and service that is available to residents
bank.explanation: Module FC requires banks to inform non-resident customers of services that may be restricted, such as loans, credit cards or cheque books, and requires enhanced due diligence for non-residents in the retail rules.

bank.question: Pearlgate uses automated monitoring for most products. A manager argues that the BD 6,000 daily-report rule therefore has no relevance to the bank. What is the best response?
options: It is only a fallback; significant transactions still need source of funds checks
The BD 6,000 rule applies only to cash deposits at branches
Automated monitoring removes any need to examine large transactions
The rule applies to every bank regardless of its systems, so all transactions over BD 6,000 must be reported to the FIU
bank.explanation: Module FC makes the BD 6,000 daily report the fallback without automated monitoring, but it still requires source of funds checks and documented examination of significant or abnormal transactions. It is not an FIU reporting threshold.

bank.question: Which situation does the CBB's risk assessment guidance list as an indicator of higher customer risk?
options: A customer who uses the bank's mobile app to check balances
A customer who pays a salary into the account every month
A company with an unusually complex ownership structure
A customer who has banked with Pearlgate for many years without any concerns
bank.explanation: The guidance lists unusual or excessively complex ownership structures, nominee shareholders, cash-intensive businesses, PEP links and negative news among higher-risk customer indicators. Regular salary payments or a long relationship are not.

bank.question: A PEP customer's first deposit arrives from a third party's account abroad. Which EDD measure in Module FC is most directly engaged?
options: Reporting the PEP to the CBB as a matter of routine
Identifying the first payment's source and a plausible explanation
Waiving the source of funds check because the PEP was already approved by senior management
Converting the account to a non-resident account
bank.explanation: Module FC's enhanced measures include specific steps to identify the source of the first payment and to ensure a plausible explanation where it was not received from the customer's own account.

bank.question: Which measures does Module FC set as the minimum for higher-risk business relationships with PEPs?
options: A personal reference from another customer and a home visit
A deposit guarantee and a reduced transaction limit
Source of wealth and funds record, senior approval, senior monitoring
A credit bureau report and an annual account statement
bank.explanation: The copy of Section FC-1.5 that could be opened requires at a minimum the source of wealth and funds record, senior management approval and senior-level ongoing monitoring for higher-risk PEP relationships.

bank.question: A private banking prospect is the business partner of a serving minister abroad and is not a public official himself. How does Module FC treat him?
options: As a standard customer, because only people who hold public office themselves are PEPs
As covered, because PEP rules reach close associates
As covered only if the minister is a Bahraini official
As covered only if he shares a joint account with the minister
bank.explanation: The copy of Section FC-1.5 that could be opened applies the requirements for all types of PEP to their family and close associates, and the CBB's guidance lists PEP links, including through beneficial owners, as a higher-risk customer factor.

bank.question: A non-face-to-face applicant passes basic document checks. Which extra measure fits Module FC's approach to non-face-to-face business?
options: Treating the applicant as low risk because technology was used
Skipping address verification for digital customers
Further steps to confirm identity and address
Requiring the CBB to approve each digital account
bank.explanation: Module FC requires specific procedures for non-face-to-face business and additional measures to ensure the customer is who they claim and the address is genuine, such as independent phone checks or employment confirmation.

bank.question: A respondent bank asks Pearlgate for 'payable-through' access so its own customers can use the account directly. What must Pearlgate confirm under Module FC?
options: That the third parties have accounts at Pearlgate as well
That it has verified the direct-access users
That the third parties are all Bahraini residents
That the respondent will deposit a security bond
bank.explanation: Among the correspondent banking factors, Module FC asks for confirmation that the respondent has verified the identity of any third parties with direct access, as in payable-through accounts.

bank.question: Pearlgate discovers that a long-standing respondent bank now provides services to a shell bank. What does Module FC point to?
options: Not knowingly continuing, and considering an STR
Asking the respondent to sign an updated questionnaire and carrying on
Moving the relationship to a different currency
Continuing the relationship, since the shell bank is not Pearlgate's own customer
bank.explanation: Module FC bars knowingly establishing relations with banks that have relations with shell banks and requires refusing to enter into or continue correspondent relationships with shell banks. A suspicion should be escalated.

bank.question: Pearlgate sends a cross-border wire for a customer. Which information must always accompany it under Module FC?
options: Only the beneficiary's name and the amount
Originator name, account and address or ID; beneficiary name and account
Only a transaction reference, since names are private
The originator's name and employer's address
bank.explanation: Module FC lists originator name, account number or IBAN where used, the originator's address, national identity number, customer identification number or date and place of birth, and the beneficiary's name and account number.

bank.question: Which statement about the source of terrorist funds matches the CBB's TF guidance?
options: Terrorist funds can be detected by looking only for large cash deposits
Terrorist funds always come from drug trafficking
Terrorist funds never pass through regulated banks
Most TF comes from seemingly legitimate sources
bank.explanation: The guidance says that one significant difference between TF and other crimes is that most TF originates from ostensibly legitimate sources, which is why ML-style red flags are not enough.

bank.question: Pearlgate's trade finance team handles a letter of credit for dual-use machinery where payment comes from a firm not named in the contract. Under the CBB's 2021 risk assessment guidance, how should this be viewed?
options: As acceptable, provided the goods are insured
As a credit risk issue only, to be handled by the lending team
As routine, because trade finance is outside AML rules
As a possible PF or sanctions evasion indicator
bank.explanation: The guidance lists dual-use goods and payments by parties not involved in the trade or not named in the letter of credit among PF and sanctions evasion indicators in trade finance.

bank.question: A relationship manager tells the MLRO that she 'knows' a client is laundering money, but her department head insists the matter is closed. Under Module FC, what must happen?
options: The department head's decision ends the matter
The relationship manager must first gather proof acceptable to a court
The report must still reach the MLRO
The client must be asked to explain before any report is made
bank.explanation: Where staff state they have knowledge or suspicion, internal consultation must not stop the report reaching the MLRO. Proof to a criminal standard is not required, and asking the client could tip him off.

bank.question: A customer's suspicious transfers involve unpaid taxes abroad. The relationship manager thinks tax matters are not for the AML team. What does Module FC say?
options: Tax-related matters are reported only to the tax authority
Report it: tax involvement makes no difference
Tax matters are reported only if the amount exceeds BD 6,000
Tax-related matters are excluded from STR reporting in Bahrain
bank.explanation: Module FC states that the duty to report suspicious transactions and attempts applies regardless of whether the transaction involves tax matters.

bank.question: After an STR is filed, the customer's son, who works at another bank, asks a Pearlgate friend whether 'anything is going on' with his father's account. What should the friend do?
options: Hint that the father should be careful with large transfers
Say nothing and tell the MLRO about the approach
Confirm that compliance is reviewing the account, since the son is in banking
Ask the son to persuade his father to explain the transfers
bank.explanation: Directors, officers and employees must not warn or inform customers or other subjects that information is being reported, and revealing an investigation can be a related offence. Telling the MLRO lets the bank manage the risk.

bank.question: What penalty range does Decree-Law No. 36 of 2017 set for the terrorist financing offence in Article 3(1-3) of Decree-Law No. 4 of 2001?
options: Up to seven years' imprisonment and a fine of up to BD 10,000
A fine of up to BD 20,000 imposed by the CBB without a court order
Up to two years' imprisonment or a fine of up to BD 50,000
Life or at least 10 years, plus BD 100,000-500,000
bank.explanation: The 2017 decree sets life imprisonment or imprisonment of not less than 10 years and a fine of BD 100,000 to BD 500,000. The BD 20,000 figure is the CBB's administrative fine under Module FC.

bank.question: Which person does the 2017 terrorist financing offence also cover, besides someone who collects funds for a terrorist group?
options: Only someone who funds a group headquartered inside Bahrain
Only someone who personally takes part in a terrorist attack
Someone who knowingly keeps such persons' funds for them
Anyone whose account receives a payment from a high-risk country
bank.explanation: The 2017 text extends the same penalty to those who obtain funds from terrorist individuals or groups for safekeeping or use in their interest, and covers groups based inside or outside Bahrain. Attempts are punished too.

bank.question: The CBB circulates an updated list of designated persons. What does Module FC expect of Pearlgate?
options: Forward the list to all customers so they can avoid listed persons
Check for dealings, report findings to the CBB, report dealings
File the list for reference and check it at the next customer review
Only act if a listed person is a Bahraini national
bank.explanation: Section FC-8.3 says the CBB issues lists, licensees verify they have no dealings and report back their findings, and any accounts or dealings are reported through the FC-5.2 procedure with later directions followed.

bank.question: A sanctions alert on a payment turns out, after checks of date of birth and nationality, to be a different person with a similar name. What is the best practice?
options: Record why the match was discounted, then release it
Block the customer permanently to avoid future alerts
Release the payment without recording anything, since it was a false match
File an STR anyway, because every alert must be reported
bank.explanation: Documented procedures for screening and handling matches, as the CBB's TF guidance expects, include recording why a potential match was discounted. Reporting is for confirmed matches or remaining suspicion, not every alert.

bank.question: Which statement about 'without delay' in UN terrorism sanctions is consistent with the CBB's TF guidance?
options: It means only after the customer has been notified
It means at the next scheduled update of the screening system
It means within 30 days of the designation
Ideally within hours of a UN designation
bank.explanation: The CBB guidance repeats FATF's reading that 'without delay' ideally means within hours of a UN designation, to prevent the flight or dissipation of funds.

bank.question: Pearlgate wants to appoint its head of corporate banking as MLRO to save costs. What does Module FC say?
options: Allowed if the head of corporate banking holds an AML qualification
Allowed for up to 120 days while a permanent MLRO is found
Allowed, provided the CBB is informed after appointment
Not allowed: a business line head role conflicts
bank.explanation: Module FC forbids combining the MLRO role with conflicting functions such as business line head or internal auditor, and requires CBB approval before appointment. The 120-day rule concerns vacancies, not conflicted appointments.

bank.question: A group wants Pearlgate's MLRO to be an employee of its overseas parent who visits Bahrain quarterly. What does Module FC say?
options: Allowed, since group functions may be shared freely
Allowed, if the parent is regulated in a FATF country
Not allowed: the MLRO must be a Bahrain-resident employee
Allowed, provided a local deputy signs STRs
bank.explanation: Module FC requires the MLRO to be a director or employee of the licensee, so the role cannot be outsourced, and to be resident in Bahrain. Delegation within a group is possible, but responsibility stays with the bank and its MLRO.

bank.question: Which access must Pearlgate give its MLRO under Module FC?
options: Access to CDD files only during the annual review
Access only to transactions over BD 6,000
Full access to transaction and CDD information
Access to customer files only with the relationship manager's consent
bank.explanation: Module FC requires the MLRO to have unrestricted access to transactional information, timely information to monitor accounts and access to all CDD information. Consent requirements would undermine independence.

bank.question: The annual review of AML/CFT effectiveness finds weak CDD on corporate customers. Under Module FC, who receives the review reports and commissions remedial measures?
options: The board, with copies to senior management
The relationship managers whose files were tested
The external auditor, who signs off the fixes
The CBB, which designs the remedial plan
bank.explanation: Module FC requires the annual compliance review reports to go to the board, which reviews them and commissions any required remedial measures, with copies to senior management.

bank.question: Which of these is a compliance record Module FC requires Pearlgate to keep for five years?
options: Minutes of every branch staff meeting
Customer satisfaction surveys
Marketing campaign results for deposit products
Reports to or by the MLRO and how they were handled
bank.explanation: Module FC requires reports made to or by the MLRO, records of how they were dealt with and what action followed, and the annual compliance review reports to be kept for five years.

bank.question: An examiner asks Pearlgate for records of a transaction completed six years ago. Under Module FC's minimum periods, what is the position?
options: The bank must ask the customer for a copy
The minimum has passed, though policy may keep them longer
The bank should never have kept them beyond one year
The bank must still hold them, because the minimum is ten years
bank.explanation: Module FC's minimum for transaction records is at least five years after completion. After six years the minimum has passed, but banks can keep records longer under their own policies or other requirements.

bank.question: Under which law do the CBB's annual reports say its conventional banking supervisors took enforcement actions, including financial penalties?
options: Article 5 of Decree-Law No. 4 of 2001
Article 38 of the CBB Law
Decree-Law No. 36 of 2017
The Policy Committee's reporting guidelines
bank.explanation: The CBB's annual reports for 2021 to 2024 state that enforcement actions by the conventional banking supervision directorates were taken as stipulated in Article 38 of the CBB Law.

bank.question: Pearlgate's head of HR proposes dropping AML targets from annual appraisals to simplify reviews. What is the issue under Module FC?
options: AML KPIs must count in all staff appraisals and pay
None, because AML KPIs apply only to the MLRO
None, because the board can waive any Module FC requirement
The CBB must first approve any change to appraisal forms
bank.explanation: Section FC-2.1 requires banks to incorporate AML/CFT KPIs for all staff and reflect performance in annual evaluations and remuneration. Boards cannot waive CBB directives.
